posts:
AI is coming for K Street lobbying. Precis AI rolls out Willard, claiming hallucination-free policy drafting via 233 databases.
Evidence: Factual Accuracy, Asymmetric Lobbying, Commercial Advantage
#Aletheia #TechPolicy #AI

Precis AI pitches Willard as an anti-hallucination safeguard for Washington policy workers, using dual AI checks across 233 government databases to ensure verified legislative data.
Stated Judgement: (+0.58, +0.62) — Lesser Good

While database grounding improves factual accuracy, the platform fundamentally accelerates bespoke influence campaigns, arming well-funded lobbyists with rapid legislative leverage.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.18, +0.52) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: COND — The Path of Revelation. Technical grounding works, but commercial lobbying automation consolidates institutional access for top spenders.
Integrity: Conditionally Sound (Hypocrisy: 1.82, z: 2)

- Precis AI Software: COND (+0.22, +0.65) — Verified database pipeline.
- Lobbying Efficiency: FAIL (-0.28, +0.55) — Power imbalance widened.
- Washington Times: PASS (+0.35, +0.40) — Direct tech reporting.
Précis AI launched Willard out of beta to supply Hill staffers and K Street firms with an AI assistant connected directly to 233 federal databases to draft policy materials without AI fabrication.

The Bright Side:
Eliminating AI hallucinations in government research prevents fabricated citations and factual errors from quietly slipping into congressional bill drafting and policy memos.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing technological precision (WHAT) with public interest (WHO). Perfect database retrieval does not democratize policy; it merely speeds up influence for elite clients.

Social Physics Analysis:
The rollout operates on a Smart Selfish Maneuver. Technologists frame high-speed database synthesis as systemic transparency, while actually entrenching private lobbying advantages over public oversight.

The Trajectory: The Path of Revelation.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Evil. Technological refinement outpaces systemic public accountability.

The Unavoidable Truth: Grounding models in government records reduces false citations.
The Unavoidable Lie: Automating lobbying analysis inherently serves the public interest.

Alethekanon:
High retrieval accuracy solves syntax errors, not power concentration. Willard streamlines legislative maneuvering for whoever pays the subscription fee.

Awwthekanon:
Accuracy in public records matters, but we must protect everyday citizens whose voices get drowned out when well-funded lobbyists get turbocharged analytical tools.

Brothekanon:
Bro built an AI that reads 233 government databases without hallucinating just so K Street can write 50-page lobbying memos in three seconds flat. Classic DC tech.

Spirithekanon:
"Woe to those who make unjust laws, to those who issue oppressive decrees." Isaiah 10:1 FAIL
Sharpening the tools of lawmaking without moral responsibility only deepens institutional harm.

As Congress debates regulations to control artificial intelligence, a Washington public relations company plans to roll out an AI tool for lobbyists and Congress staff that promises to stop the technology from making things up.

[Précis AI](/topics/precis-ai/), the company behind Willard, said the AI tool grounds answers in government databases, with a second AI model checking the work to avoid the fabricated citations that have plagued general-purpose chatbots.
